title: Oscar and the Will
premise: Ada Yarrow, an insurance investigator whose photographic memory has made him both invaluable and isolated, receives two letters about the same man: one confessing to the drowning death of Oscar Vane ten years ago, the other promising a second death is coming. When Ada discovers Oscar's life insurance policy was never paid out because the body was never found, he reopens the case in the river town of Hallowmere, where everyone who signed the original file now lives under new names. As Ada's memory reconstructs the night of the drowning, he realizes Oscar faked his own death, that the confessing letter-writer is dying and wants absolution, and that the second letter promises to kill Oscar for real. In the end Ada finds Oscar alive but unrecognizable, must choose between exposing him or protecting the town's fragile peace, and finally lets the second letter's sender — Oscar's twin brother — carry out the promise, closing the case at the cost of Ada's certainty that memory can ever be trusted.
about_author: Dominic Okafor is a former claims adjuster from Port Harcourt who spent eleven years reading other people's accounts of how things ended before turning to fiction. He writes mysteries about paperwork, memory, and the lies people sign their names to.

chapters.title: Two Envelopes, One Hand
chapters.summary: Ada Yarrow, sorting cold files in his London office, receives two letters postmarked from Hallowmere: one confessing to murder, one promising 'the rest of him by spring.' Both are written in the same handwriting — a hand Ada recognizes from a closed 2014 file. POV: Ada. Emotional beat: unease sharpening into obsession as his photographic memory locks onto the letters.

chapters.title: The File That Won't Stay Shut
chapters.summary: Ada pulls the archived Vane case: Oscar Vane, drowned in the River Meld, body never recovered, claim denied. His supervisor, Ruth Okonkwo, orders him to drop it; the denial was upheld twice. That night Ada recites the file verbatim from memory and notices a witness statement with a time stamp impossible for the tide. POV: Ada. Beat: quiet defiance.

chapters.title: Hallowmere
chapters.summary: Ada arrives in the rain-soaked river town where the floodgates open on schedule and everyone watches strangers too closely. He checks into a boarding house run by Marta Quill, who mistakes him for someone named 'Ellis.' POV: Ada, with a brief interlude of Marta's wary observations. Beat: displacement — Ada, who remembers everything, is somewhere no one wants anything remembered.

chapters.title: The Widow Who Isn't
chapters.summary: Ada tracks down Oscar's widow, Sylvie Vane, now remarried to the town's flood engineer, Daniel Cray. She denies receiving any letters but her hands shake when Ada quotes the confession aloud. Her young son wears a locket engraved with a date three years after the drowning. POV: Ada. Beat: the first crack — grief that doesn't match its official story.

chapters.title: What the Tide Keeps
chapters.summary: Ada walks the riverbank at low water and finds a rusted watch wedged in the reeds, stopped at 11:47 — the exact minute in the denied claim. The watch's engraving reads 'O.V., from T.V.' A local boy warns him people have drowned looking for keepsakes here. POV: Ada. Beat: dread; the river is returning evidence on its own schedule.

chapters.title: Tobias Vane
chapters.summary: Records reveal Oscar had a twin brother, Tobias, presumed dead in a car crash two years after the drowning. Ada cross-references handwriting samples: the letters match Tobias's known writing. But Tobias died — so who wrote them? POV: Ada, intercut with a flashback fragment of two boys on the river. Beat: vertigo; the case now has a ghost at its center.

chapters.title: The Man Called Ellis
chapters.summary: Marta Quill admits 'Ellis' was a lodger five years ago — quiet, scarred, gone without paying. She shows Ada a sketch Ellis left behind: it's Oscar's face, older. Someone in town has been hiding him, and Marta knows more than she'll say. POV: Marta, then Ada. Beat: tenderness and complicity — Marta protected a broken man out of kindness.

chapters.title: Signed Statements
chapters.summary: Ada interviews the surviving witnesses from the original file: a lockkeeper, a retired constable, and Dr. Fenwick, who certified the death. Each account differs from what they signed in 2014 — and each difference matches something only an insider would know. POV: Ada. Beat: mounting paranoia; the closed case was stitched shut by many hands.

chapters.title: The Confessor
chapters.summary: A second letter arrives at Ada's boarding house: 'You're close. Ask Fenwick about the boat.' Ada confronts Dr. Fenwick, who breaks down and admits he falsified the death certificate — but insists he did it to protect someone, not to bury a crime. POV: Ada. Beat: moral fog; every lie so far was told as mercy.

chapters.title: Spring Tide
chapters.summary: Ruth calls: the insurance company is sending its own investigator, Callum Reeve, to shut Ada down. Reeve arrives charming and ruthless, and it emerges he handled the original denial. Ada realizes the company may have suspected fraud all along and buried it. POV: Ada, then Reeve's smooth internal calculations. Beat: institutional menace enters the story.

chapters.title: The Locket
chapters.summary: Ada gets the boy's locket date confirmed: it's the anniversary of Tobias's car crash. Sylvie has been mourning both brothers in secret. Under pressure she admits Oscar came back once, three years ago, stood in her garden, and left before dawn. POV: Sylvie. Beat: heartbreak — a love split between a living ghost and a dead one.

chapters.title: Under the Floodgate
chapters.summary: Following the lockkeeper's altered statement, Ada searches beneath the old floodgate and finds a hidden skiff, dry-rotted but recently patched. Someone has been using the river at night. Fresh oil on the pulley. POV: Ada. Beat: hunter's thrill curdling into fear — he's being watched from the tree line.

chapters.title: Reeve's Offer
chapters.summary: Callum Reeve offers Ada a promotion to walk away, revealing the company paid Sylvie a private settlement years ago on condition of silence. Refusing means ending his career. Ada refuses; that night his hotel room is searched and his copy of the confession stolen. POV: Ada. Beat: isolation deepens; the price of survival begins to show its bill.

chapters.title: The Night Swimmer
chapters.summary: Ada stakes out the skiff and sees a figure rowing upstream through the dark — broad-shouldered, limping. He follows along the bank and loses him at the derelict boathouse, but finds wet footprints and a cigarette brand Oscar favored. POV: Ada. Beat: confirmation and terror in equal measure; Oscar is alive.

chapters.title: Oscar
chapters.summary: In the boathouse Ada finally meets Oscar Vane — gaunt, half-deaf from the cold-water years, living off the river and Marta's charity. Oscar confesses everything: he staged the drowning to escape debts and a violent creditor, letting his brother take the blame trail. He begs Ada to let the past stay past. POV: Oscar. Beat: pity warring with duty; the survivor's cost laid bare.

chapters.title: The Second Letter Explained
chapters.summary: Oscar reveals the truth: Tobias didn't die in the crash — he survived disfigured, blamed Oscar for abandoning him, and has been writing the letters himself. 'The rest of him by spring' means Tobias intends to kill Oscar when the spring tide comes. Oscar won't run again. POV: Ada, with Tobias's letter fragments interleaved. Beat: the mystery inverts into a countdown.

chapters.title: Where Brothers Drown
chapters.summary: Ada traces Tobias to a caravan outside town and confronts him. Tobias is dying of illness — the confession letter was his attempt at absolution before death, the threat his attempt at justice. He gives Ada until the spring tide to decide which brother survives the story. POV: Tobias. Beat: devastating symmetry; both brothers are ghosts of the same night.

chapters.title: What Memory Is For
chapters.summary: Ada, unable to sleep, replays every detail he's memorized and finally sees what he missed: the original witness statements weren't covering a murder — they were covering Oscar's escape route, coordinated by Sylvie and Fenwick out of love. The town didn't hide a crime; it hid a rescue. POV: Ada. Beat: revelation as grief — the truth dissolves his certainty.

chapters.title: The Spring Tide
chapters.summary: On the night of the highest tide, Tobias goes to the boathouse. Ada races ahead and finds the brothers face to face — Oscar offering his life, Tobias unable to take it. Reeve arrives with police tipped by an anonymous letter. In the chaos, Tobias collapses. POV: Ada. Beat: climax — violence threatened, then undone by exhaustion and love.

chapters.title: One Death, Properly Counted
chapters.summary: Tobias dies at dawn in the boathouse, holding Oscar's hand, his confession finally true in every particular. Ada must decide what to write in his report. Reeve offers to bury everything if Oscar disappears forever. POV: Ada. Beat: the price of survival comes due — someone must be erased for anyone to live.

chapters.title: The Report
chapters.summary: Ada files his finding: Oscar Vane deceased, remains unrecoverable, claim closed. He burns the letters, keeps only the stopped watch, and tells Sylvie nothing except that she owes no one an explanation. Oscar leaves Hallowmere on the morning boat, alive and officially drowned. POV: Ada. Beat: bittersweet resolution; belonging purchased with a lie.

chapters.title: What Ada Keeps
chapters.summary: Months later, back in London, Ada receives a blank postcard from a coastal town — no words, just proof of life. He pins it above his desk beside the watch. For the first time, he chooses not to memorize a detail: he lets the postmark blur. POV: Ada. Beat: quiet coda — memory as a burden he finally learns to set down.
